name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 28

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Hike to support hounds

blocks.note: to support someone is to back them
hounds hunt together as a pack

explanation.surface: A walker sets off on a long hike to keep up with a hunt's hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to go walking cross-country carrying your kit on your shoulders, a kind of long hike.

clue.text: Talk of bed and breakfast being included in the package

indicators.note: being included in means one item sits inside the wrapping of the other

blocks.note: a bale is a large bound bundle
B and B is the standard short form of bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: Chat about a holiday deal that includes bed and breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To babble is to talk rapidly and foolishly, a kind of chatter.

clue.text: Song vehicle achieving original ends

indicators.note: ends picks out only the first and final letters of the word before it

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
the first and final letters of this word

explanation.surface: A van's tune that manages to sound new at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a joyful hymn, especially one sung at Christmas, so a kind of song.

clue.text: You've had it!

blocks.note: surface reading: a threat that someone is finished or in trouble
setter's reading: you have succeeded in an examination, or the ball is handed on

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like doom; read instead as congratulation after a test, or handing something over.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting through an exam is described with this word, and handing a ball to a teammate is also this.

clue.text: Many moving around line on map

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
travelling from place to place is being on tour

explanation.surface: Crowds wandering past a line drawn on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: On a relief map, a curve joining points of equal height is called by this term.

clue.text: I'm accustomed to be entertained

blocks.note: I'm expands to I am; the verb part is kept
accustomed to something means used to it

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to always being the one who is kept amused.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm accustomed' as 'I am used': drop the I and the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amused has been diverted and made to smile, which is what being entertained means.

clue.text: Some difficulty about finding ring for an animal

indicators.note: a word in difficulty and pushed about is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to find a ring for a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring's letter joins the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a very large deer of northern forests, called an elk in Europe.

clue.text: Diminutive employee providing quick note

blocks.note: something diminutive is small or short
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A small worker hands over a brief memo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a system of abbreviated symbols for taking down speech fast, so a way of noting quickly.

clue.text: One taking off for the Sahara?

definitions.text: One taking off for the Sahara?

blocks.clueFragment: One taking off for the Sahara?
blocks.note: surface reading: a traveller departing for the great African sand sea
setter's reading: a soldier running away from the army, read as if tied to dry wastelands

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: someone who absconds sounds like someone heading for arid wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who abandons their post and runs off is the person described, here punning on the sandy wasteland.

clue.text: Those that can fly on to good country sound

blocks.note: creatures with wings that take to the air
taken as written
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Fliers heading off towards a pleasant land, a migration story.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds singing is the typical noise heard in rural surroundings, away from towns and traffic.

clue.text: River turning sour and spongy

indicators.note: something turning is moved round, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A river going sour and turning boggy, as after pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Spongy material is full of small holes that let water soak through, which is exactly what porous describes.

clue.text: Finally get run out in an act

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the next word
out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer is finally run out mid-performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a single performer's slot in a variety show, the same as an act.

clue.text: White flower girl

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall plant with large pale trumpet blooms
second meaning: a female first name

explanation.surface: A young woman in white, like a bride or a flower girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna lily is a classic white bloom, and the same word is a common given name for women.

clue.text: Idle one turning to employment after a time outside

indicators.note: turning round means the small word just after it is read backwards
outside says the time word wraps round the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: after a while is later
the short word to be read backwards
employing something is putting it to use

explanation.surface: A layabout finally turns to work after a long time out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' tells you the time word is split open to take the rest. The lotus-eaters in Homer's Odyssey ate a fruit that left them dreamily idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotus-eater is a person living in lazy, dreamy indulgence, so an idle sort of person.

clue.text: Present the lady with some dope

blocks.note: the lady is referred to as her
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman is offered a gift along with a quantity of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying here at a roll call shows a person is in attendance, which is what present means.

clue.text: Consents to provide drink where bargains are to be had

definitions.text: where bargains are to be had

blocks.note: official permissions or approvals are clearances
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Permission granted to serve drinks at a venue known for bargains.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop clearing its stock sells it off cheaply, so it is a place to find goods at reduced prices.

clue.text: Money needed for a true mixed drink

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the preceding words' letters are reordered

blocks.note: coin is cash
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cash is required for a properly made cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, served as a drink or used in cocktails.

clue.text: Wonder what's in the top drawer

indicators.note: what's in asks for letters sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the last word

explanation.surface: Curiosity about the contents of the highest drawer in a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a feeling of reverent amazement, the same sense as wonder used as a noun.

clue.text: Animal not dead showing vigour

indicators.note: not dead says the abbreviation for dead is taken away

blocks.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A creature still alive and full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is energetic style and enthusiasm, so it shares the meaning of vigour.

clue.text: Word play one dropped when given correction

blocks.note: a joke on a double meaning
I is the Roman numeral one
to drop something is to shed it

explanation.surface: A teacher strikes out a pun when marking an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punished means receiving a penalty, which is correction in the sense of discipline.

clue.text: Joined in upright declaration of strength together

blocks.note: things joined together are united
if we are in an upright position, we stand

explanation.surface: A rallying motto spoken by people joined together and standing tall.
explanation.walkthrough: The full slogan runs 'United we stand, divided we fall'.
explanation.definitionFit: The motto proclaims that a group is strong when its members act as one, a statement of collective solidarity.

clue.text: A little bit slow to end with success

indicators.note: to end points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
a success is a hit

explanation.surface: Something a little sluggish at first finally succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit', so a tiny bit.

clue.text: That woman called to get a drink here?

blocks.note: that woman is she
having called on someone means having been to see them

explanation.surface: A woman pays a visit hoping for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, a word from Irish and Scottish English and South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit drink is sold in a shebeen, so it is a place where alcohol can be had.

clue.text: Preservation with no falling back

blocks.note: not falling behind is keeping up, and back says its two words swap places

explanation.surface: Maintenance work that stops a building slipping into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No falling back' is the phrase keep up; reading it back to front word by word puts up before keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the maintenance of a building or property in good condition, which is preservation.

clue.text: Tennis ties arranged for some insiders

indicators.note: matches are arranged into an order, so these letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A club secretary sets up tennis fixtures for members in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insiders' looks like people in the know; here it means things literally inside you.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowels sit inside the body, so they are a playful example of things that are inside.

clue.text: Time needed to provide appropriate letters

blocks.note: first meaning: a period
second meaning: to write out a word correctly

explanation.surface: Someone needs time to write suitable correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a stretch of time, and to spell is to give the right characters in order for a word.

clue.text: Stern work for RAF officer

blocks.note: PO is a Pilot Officer in the Royal Air Force
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A stiff task handed to an air force officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective meaning strict; it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the raised deck at the rear of a ship, so it is found at the stern.

clue.text: Rosie's willowy form

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a willow, not the adjective

indicators.note: form suggests shaping into a new figure, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Rosie has a slim, graceful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: See if you can compete and start winning

indicators.note: start keeps just the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: to vie is to compete
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A challenge to find out whether you can take part and win.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to look at it, which is a sense of see.

clue.text: Listed as having been sole associate

blocks.note: first meaning: tilted over to one side, as a ship does
second meaning: fitted with the part of a shoe that partners the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone named on a register as a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole associate' reads as only partner; here it is the shoe part that goes with the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels leans over, as one that lists does; a heeled shoe has its rear piece attached beside the sole.

clue.text: Wanting to feel better, one takes it

definitions.text: Wanting to feel better, one takes it

blocks.clueFragment: Wanting to feel better, one takes it
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who wants to feel better grabs at something
setter's reading: what a patient swallows to recover from illness

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone seeking comfort or advantage; the thing taken is a remedy for sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person hoping to recover swallows a dose of a drug prescribed for the illness.

clue.text: Run to get a big drink

blocks.note: first meaning: to move at a jog
second meaning: a twice-sized measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone dashes to the bar to get a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: To double is to run quickly, as soldiers do; a double is two standard measures of a spirit poured together.

clue.text: Point to present fall in plant life

definitions.note: the answer is one plant, not plant life in general

blocks.note: S is south, a compass point
the present moment is now
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A lecturer points to a current decline in the world's plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white-flowered bulb that blooms in late winter, an example of a plant.
